note: Lines of the 0.7.0 standards changed on purpose during the 1.0.0 migration, each with its reason. The line-conservation check allows exactly these and nothing else. Heading lines that only gained a {#id} are not listed.

lines.before: 3. **One home per rule.** A rule lives in this file only. Memory, notes, briefs and tracking files hold a pointer (`-> _Working Standards.md "Section"`), never a restated copy. Why: two copies drift, and the stale one gets followed. *Check: tests flag kit memory lines that repeat this file's wording.*
lines.after: 3. **One home per rule.** A rule lives in one rule module, under one heading with a fixed ID. Memory, notes, briefs and tracking files hold a pointer (`-> rule:<id>`, the fixed ID after the rule's heading), never a restated copy. Why: two copies drift, and the stale one gets followed. *Check: tests flag kit memory lines that repeat this file's wording.*
lines.why: The pointer form changed to the rule ID; the old form is what the link check now refuses. The standards became rule modules.

added.line: 11. **One source, written out per tool.** Rules are edited only in the kit's `rules/` (plain Markdown with neutral frontmatter: id, load, paths, when, tags); `kit.mjs build` writes each tool's files - today Claude Code's `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/rules/` and `standards/`. Each tool's output names the docs it follows and is re-checked against them at every kit release. Why: one tool-neutral source lets any AI use the rules, and a hand edit to a written-out copy is overwritten. *Check: the build-freshness test.*
